bend, be bent (mghongo ghwake ghokuchika 'his back is bent')
exceed, be too much (cha-bi-a 'it is too much'; vi-da-biy-a)
be married (of a woman): passive of lowola 'marry'
depend on, rely on (Swahili loan tegemea)
plant (crops/trees): kuwa tindi 'plant tomatoes', kuwa pemba 'plant maize'
be played (loan cheza, passive); the native verb for 'play' is sarigha (wawesarigha, sarigha kushinde), and vina 'dance'
bed (loan kitanda + LOC -nyi: kitandenyi); native wuli (wulinyi)
be satisfied (ndedikato 'we are not (yet) satisfied', nde-di-kat-o with passive-perfective -o)
has not (yet) died: NEG.ja nde-u-fu-e (nde + u -> ndou/ndeu); root fwa 'die'
get along, agree (lit. 'hear each other', sikira + reciprocal -an-)
